title: Ecclesiastes — Instructions and Commands
content:
Ecclesiastes — Instructions and Commands

Instructions · All Old Testament books · Original Torah and New Testament index

24 additional passage records · 31 quoted verse units. Read Ecclesiastes in Saints Translation.

This is a working instruction register organized by topic and then classification. Open a passage for its exact wording, source link and context note. Historical orders and rhetorical or poetic addresses retain their original setting; their presence here does not make them universal laws.

Review status: Working catalogue: the source collection covers every Old Testament book currently in Saints.Bible. Individual commands, repeated formulations, speakers and Christian application still require further review; this is not a certified exhaustive count of laws.

Topics: Faith, repentance and allegiance · Worship, prayer and holy things · Justice, truth and protection · Family, marriage and household · Wisdom, speech and conduct · Historical commissions, journeys and public life

Faith, repentance and allegiance

Uncertain · 7 passage records

Ecclesiastes 5:5 – Ecclesiastes 5:6

Record type: Wisdom instruction. Source section: Do Not Be Hasty with Your Mouth.

Ecclesiastes 5:5 — Do not let your mouth cause your flesh to sin, and do not say before God, “It was ignorance,” lest God become angry at your voice and destroy the works of your hands.

Ecclesiastes 5:6 — For with many dreams come futilities and many words; therefore fear God.

Context and scope: Wisdom counsel in its original setting. Continuing application and any correspondence with the New Testament are not automatically assigned.

Ecclesiastes 7:13 – Ecclesiastes 7:14

Record type: Wisdom instruction. Source section: Consider God's Works.

Ecclesiastes 7:13 — Consider God’s works, for who can put in order the one whom God has twisted?

Ecclesiastes 7:14 — On a day of goodness, live in good; on a day of evil, consider: God has made this in accord with that concerning speech, so that human beings may find out nothing that comes after them.

Context and scope: Wisdom counsel in its original setting. Continuing application and any correspondence with the New Testament are not automatically assigned.

Ecclesiastes 7:17 — Do not be greatly ungodly, and do not become harsh, lest you die before your time.

Ecclesiastes 7:18 — It is good for you to hold to this and also not release your hand from that, for the one who fears God will come through them all.
